newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening mixed to higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening mixed to higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open mixed to higher Friday after a week of steady gains.
Analysts said the market may be poised for some profit-taking following the Dow's 136-point surge to a close at 7711 Thursday.
Investors will take their cue from the Producer Price Index figures for May, due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, the analysts said.
The data are expected to show a mild increase of 0.1 percent, after four months of declines, according to economists surveyed by Reuters.
"That is going to be affecting trading when that comes out," said Hildegard Zagorski, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
"I would expect that you might run into some profit-taking today, but again for the long term the outlook is very good," she said.
The benchmark 30-year long bond was up 4/32 with a 6.77 percent yield. The Standard & Poor's futures index was off one to 894.10.

The market rallied Thursday after the release of weaker-than-expected retail sales data for May. Investors took the 0.1 percent decline in retail sales, as well as an increase in new jobless claims, as a sign the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates at its July meeting.
Japan's Nikkei average closed lower, down 36.11 points, or 0.18 percent, at 20,528.35.
In London the FTSE 100 was up 29.1 points at 4786.5. U.S. stocks trading in London rose on momentum from the Dow's fifth straight record high close yesterday.
The dollar was steady against the yen in Tokyo after erasing earlier gains. The U.S. currency stood at 114.19/29 yen. In Europe the dollar was trading at 1.7300/10 marks.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that times have changed at J.P. Morgan & Co, where there is new interest in the mutual fund business, a shift from the bank's typical high-priced clients.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that the initial public offering of Polo Ralph Lauren Corp RL.N was very successful but, according to some analysts, left the stock overvalued.
